name: Notion
tagline: The connected workspace for notes, docs, and projects
description: Notion is an all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. GAIA is a proactive AI assistant that orchestrates your email, calendar, tasks, and the rest of your tools — and integrates directly with Notion to read and write your pages and databases.
metaTitle: Notion vs GAIA: Source-Available AI That Acts
metaDescription: Notion vs GAIA: Notion tracks work you enter by hand; GAIA triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across your tools. Source-available with a free tier.
intro: Notion has become the default workspace for millions of individuals and teams. Its flexible blocks, powerful databases, and polished doc editor make it the go-to place to capture knowledge, plan projects, and build internal wikis. But Notion is fundamentally a place you go to write and organise — it waits for you to open it. GAIA takes the opposite approach: it monitors your email, calendar, and connected tools continuously, acts on your behalf before you ask, and integrates directly with Notion so your workspace stays in sync with everything happening around it. Where Notion organises information, GAIA orchestrates work.

rows.gaia: Proactive AI productivity OS that monitors and acts across email, calendar, tasks, and the rest of your tools on your behalf
rows.competitor: All-in-one connected workspace for notes, docs, wikis, and project databases that you build and maintain manually

rows.gaia: AI-powered todos with semantic search, priorities, projects, and deadlines: tasks created automatically from emails and conversations
rows.competitor: Database-backed task tracking with custom properties, filters, and views (board, list, calendar, gallery); requires manual entry

rows.gaia: Full Gmail management: triages inbox, drafts replies, converts emails into tasks or Notion pages automatically
rows.competitor: No native email integration or inbox management; emails can be clipped manually via the Notion Web Clipper browser extension

rows.gaia: Ambient AI that proactively summarises threads, prepares meeting briefs, writes drafts, detects priorities, and orchestrates cross-tool actions without prompting
rows.competitor: Notion AI (add-on) assists with writing, summarising, translating, and filling database fields within the Notion editor on demand

rows.gaia: Natural language multi-step workflows with triggers, conditions, and actions spanning any connected tool: created by describing what you want in plain English
rows.competitor: Built-in database automations (e.g., notify on status change, create pages from templates); advanced cross-tool automation requires Zapier or Make

rows.gaia: Continuously monitors email, calendar, and connected tools to surface insights and take action before you ask
rows.competitor: Passive workspace: notifies you of page comments and mentions; does not monitor external context or act proactively

rows.gaia: Full Google Calendar integration: reads, creates, and updates events; prepares briefings before meetings automatically
rows.competitor: Calendar view for Notion databases; limited Google Calendar sync available; no proactive meeting preparation

rows.gaia: Graph-based persistent memory that links tasks, projects, meetings, emails, documents, and people for deep contextual understanding over time
rows.competitor: Knowledge is stored as pages and databases within your workspace; connections are made via backlinks and relations you create manually

rows.gaia: MCP integrations including Notion, Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Jira, and more: all orchestrated by the AI agent
rows.competitor: Native integrations with Slack, GitHub, Jira, Figma, and Google Drive; broader ecosystem available via Zapier, Make, and the Notion API

rows.gaia: Source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial) and self-hostable via Docker: your data stays in your own infrastructure
rows.competitor: Proprietary closed-source SaaS platform; no self-hosting option available

rows.gaia: Free tier available; Pro from ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month; self-hosting free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs) with no per-seat cost
rows.competitor: Free plan and paid plans available; per-seat pricing; enterprise tiers available.

gaiaAdvantages: Proactively reads your email and creates tasks, Notion pages, or calendar events automatically: no manual capture required
Acts before you ask: surfaces what needs attention across email, calendar, and tools without waiting to be opened
Natural language multi-step workflows that span your entire tool stack, including writing back to Notion databases
Graph-based persistent memory builds a living map of your projects, people, and decisions across every tool you use
Source-available and self-hostable: complete data ownership with no per-seat pricing when self-hosted
competitorAdvantages: Exceptionally flexible block-based editor for building docs, wikis, databases, and internal tools with a polished UI
Powerful relational databases with custom properties, multiple views, and filters: ideal for structured knowledge management
Established ecosystem of templates, integrations, and a large community for every use case from personal notes to company wikis
verdict: Choose Notion if your primary need is a flexible workspace to write docs, build wikis, and organise structured knowledge with your team — Notion's editor and database system are genuinely best-in-class for that job. Choose GAIA if you want an AI assistant that works proactively across your email, calendar, and tools — creating content in Notion for you, automating repetitive cross-tool workflows, and maintaining a persistent understanding of your work without manual input. The most effective setup uses both: Notion as your knowledge base and GAIA as the AI layer that keeps it connected to everything happening in your digital life.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with Notion?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA integrates with Notion via MCP and can read and write pages, databases, and tasks in your Notion workspace using natural language. You can ask GAIA to create a Notion page from a meeting summary, update a database record, or surface content from your Notion wiki — all without opening Notion directly.

faqs.question: Can GAIA replace Notion for note-taking and documentation?
faqs.answer: GAIA's strength is orchestration and proactive action rather than rich document editing. For teams that depend on Notion's flexible block editor, relational databases, and wiki structure, GAIA works best as a complement — acting as the AI layer that populates and updates Notion content automatically rather than replacing the workspace itself.

faqs.question: How is GAIA different from Notion AI?
faqs.answer: Notion AI is an in-editor assistant that helps you write, summarise, and edit content within Notion pages on demand. GAIA is a proactive agent that operates across your entire digital environment — reading your email, managing your calendar, triggering automations, and writing to Notion as one of many connected tools. Notion AI enhances what you do inside Notion; GAIA orchestrates what happens across everything, including Notion.

faqs.question: Is GAIA cheaper than Notion for teams?
faqs.answer: For larger teams, GAIA's self-hosting option removes per-seat pricing entirely — you cover only your own hosting and model API costs. Notion's Business plan charges per seat billed annually, which scales quickly with headcount. GAIA's hosted Pro plan starts at ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month regardless of seat count, and self-hosting is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs).
